description: Apollo Tales é uma equipe dedicada a transformar a história da exploração espacial em uma experiência educacional interativa. Para o NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, estamos desenvolvendo um jogo de exploração web em 2D onde os jogadores descobrem equipamentos abandonados da NASA na Lua e em Marte, revelando a ciência e a história por trás das missões espaciais de forma lúdica.
summary:
Lunar Odyssey is an educational, top-down pixel-art game created for the challenge "Abandoned but Not Forgotten: Storytelling about NASA's Discarded Equipment on the Moon and Mars." This MVP focuses on equipment left on the Moon. Players take the role of an astronaut on a reconnaissance mission whose ship is damaged during landing. To repair it and return to Earth, they explore the Moon and its real equipment, the Surveyor 3 lander and a radioisotope thermoelectric generator (RTG), and learn what each one did through short narrated stories, historical images and quick quiz questions. Every discovery rewards the player with a real component that repairs the ship, so learning and progress go hand in hand.

Sources about past space missions are often dense and technical, which discourages younger and first-time audiences. Our MVP presents accurate, source-based content in a playful, accessible format, available in English and Portuguese, lowering the barrier to entry. It matters because curiosity about space history can inspire the next generation of explorers, and these stories should not stay forgotten on the Moon.
details:
WHAT IT DOES AND HOW IT WORKS

Lunar Odyssey puts the player in the role of an astronaut whose ship is damaged on the Moon. To repair it, the player walks across a top down lunar map, by clicking or using the keyboard, to visit two real pieces of NASA equipment left on the surface: the Surveyor 3 lander (1967) and a radioisotope thermoelectric generator (RTG), the "nuclear battery" that powered the Apollo science stations.

At each one, an astronaut character narrates its real history in short speech bubbles, with voice narration and historical images. Before each reward, the player answers a quick multiple choice question. Right or wrong, the player receives the part, and a wrong answer shows the correct explanation right away.

In total, there are 2 pieces of equipment, 4 questions and 4 parts that fill a repair bar: the TV camera system and the soil scoop (Surveyor 3), and the thermocouples and the power conditioning unit (RTG). Once the bar is full, the player returns to the ship and watches it take off for Earth.

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

The game turns dense technical documents into short, playful stories for young and first time audiences. Learning is active: players interpret information, are rewarded for discovering it, and recall it through questions. The game is available in English and Portuguese, with an instant language switch and voice narration in both. We hope it makes people curious about the history of space exploration and shows that forgotten artifacts still have stories worth telling.

TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGY

Built with React 19, TypeScript and Vite, styled with Tailwind CSS, with retro sound effects generated through the Web Audio API and deployed on Firebase Hosting.

The team used AI tools throughout development: Google AI Studio generated code and the pixel art images; ElevenLabs produced the voices (text to speech narration in English and Portuguese); Claude turned NASA technical documents about the Surveyor 3 and the RTG into short texts, quiz questions and narration scripts; and Google Antigravity, ChatGPT/Codex and Gemini worked as programming assistants. The team reviewed all historical facts against the source documents.

CREATIVITY

Instead of presenting the artifacts as a catalog, we made the player's own progress depend on them: each piece of equipment gives the player a part, so the story of the equipment is the game's progress. An astronaut narrator passes the knowledge on as if guiding the player through the Moon's history, wrapped in a 16 bit pixel art style.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

Scientific accuracy: we based all facts on NASA source documents and reviewed them carefully, avoiding claims they do not support. We made clear that the RTG is neither a bomb nor a fission reactor, and the player never touches its fuel. The repair mechanic is a narrative device. We also considered age appropriate language, short narrations that fit in speech bubbles, flexible controls (mouse and keyboard) and full bilingual support.
